name: ble_gatt_reassembly
description: BLE GATT frame reassembly conformance vectors for the two GATT transports: KISS-over-BLE (TNC apps) and Meshtastic-compatible GATT (4-byte length-prefix chunked writes). All byte sequences are hand-derived from framing rules (RFC-style KISS escaping, protobuf wire format) and are independent of any implementation output.
spec: spec/kiss-framing.md section 5.5 (BLE KISS GATT), BLE-KISS-API (aprs.fi), Meshtastic BLE wire format as mirrored in python/src/lichen/interface/meshtastic/gatt.py and rust lichen-meshtastic/src/gatt.rs
scope_notes: BLE ATT/GATT delivers writes reliably and in order within a single connection, so out-of-order fragment arrival is not a scenario defined by either profile; reconnection state-reset is covered instead (kiss_reconnect_clears_partial_reassembly, meshtastic_disconnect_discards_partial).
Interleaved fragments from multiple simultaneous GATT clients are likewise undefined for these single-client characteristics; sequential connections stand in for the multiple-connection requirement.

A KISS frame whose escaped length exceeds kiss_max_frame_size (2048) is not enforced per-frame by the current Python reader (only the stream-buffer memory guard is); see kiss_oversized_garbage_discarded for the enforced guard behavior.

vectors.name: kiss_happy_path_exact_mtu
vectors.description: Port 0 DATA frame 'LICHEN-BLE-KISS-01' whose wire form is exactly 20 bytes (DEFAULT_MTU); delivered in a single characteristic write.
vectors.oracle_note: Wire form hand-built: FEND, CMD 0x00 (port 0, DATA), unescaped ASCII payload, FEND.

vectors.name: kiss_split_across_writes
vectors.description: 37-byte frame 'frame-boundaries-across-mtu-writes' split into a 20-byte and a 17-byte write; reassembled into exactly one frame.
vectors.oracle_note: Split point chosen at the 20-byte MTU boundary falling mid-payload; no escapes present (all printable ASCII).

vectors.name: kiss_escaped_payload
vectors.description: Payload containing FEND, FESC, TFEND, TFESC bytes survives escaping across reassembly: c0->db dc, db->db dd, literals pass through.
vectors.oracle_note: Escaped body db dc db dd dc dd decodes back to c0 db dc dd by the two transposition rules alone.

vectors.name: kiss_two_frames_single_write
vectors.description: Two complete frames concatenated inside one write yield two frames in order ('alpha', then 'beta!').
vectors.oracle_note: Frame boundary is the closing FEND; the reader must resync at it rather than treat the pair as one frame.

vectors.name: kiss_garbage_prefix_resync
vectors.description: Leading non-FEND garbage before the first FEND is discarded during sync; exactly the valid trailing frame is delivered.
vectors.oracle_note: Sync rule: bytes before the first FEND carry no framing semantics.

vectors.name: kiss_inter_frame_fend_padding
vectors.description: Consecutive FENDs around a frame (inter-frame padding) produce a single frame, not empty ones.
vectors.oracle_note: FEND FEND content FEND FEND collapses to one delimited frame per KISS delimiter semantics.

vectors.name: kiss_partial_frame_completed_by_later_write
vectors.description: An unterminated frame prefix emits nothing; the completing write finishes exactly one frame with the full payload 'hello'.
vectors.oracle_note: Partial-frame handling: no output until the closing FEND; payload is the concatenation across writes.

vectors.name: kiss_truncated_escape_frame_skipped
vectors.description: A frame ending in a lone FESC before its closing FEND is malformed (truncated escape sequence); it is dropped and the stream recovers so the following frame still parses.
vectors.oracle_note: Escape rule requires a partner byte after db; db followed by the closing FEND cannot decode, so that frame is discarded without affecting the next.

vectors.name: kiss_oversized_garbage_discarded
vectors.description: A 5000-byte FEND-less garbage run exceeds the stream-buffer memory guard (2 x max_frame_size = 4096) and is discarded wholesale; a subsequent valid frame is delivered intact.
vectors.oracle_note: Memory-guard rule: a buffer with no FEND-delimited progress beyond twice max_frame_size must be dropped to bound memory; writes arrive MTU-sized (250 x 20 B).

vectors.name: kiss_large_valid_frame_under_limit
vectors.description: A legitimate 1500-byte unescaped payload yields a 1503-byte frame, under the documented 2048-byte escaped-size limit; delivered as 76 MTU-sized writes and reassembled losslessly.
vectors.oracle_note: Envelope hand-derived (FEND CMD payload FEND); chunking at the 20-byte MTU is mechanical; 1503 <= 2048 so the frame is admissible.

vectors.name: kiss_reconnect_clears_partial_reassembly
vectors.description: A partially received frame is abandoned on disconnect; after reconnect the stream starts clean and only the new connection's frame is delivered.
vectors.oracle_note: Sequential multiple-connection scenario: reassembly state is per-connection; the abandoned 'cafe' prefix must never surface.

vectors.name: meshtastic_complete_in_single_chunk
vectors.description: Header declaring 4 payload bytes followed by the full payload arrives in one write; ToRadio(want_config_id=69420) parses immediately.
vectors.oracle_note: Header 04 00 00 00 (uint16 LE length 4 + two reserved zero bytes); payload 18 ac 9e 04 is field 3 varint 69420 by protobuf wire rules (tag 0x18 = field 3 varint; 69420 = 0xac,0x9e,0x04 base-128 groups).

vectors.name: meshtastic_byte_by_byte_reassembly
vectors.description: The same message delivered one byte per write: seven writes yield no message, the eighth completes it.
vectors.oracle_note: Reassembly must be indifferent to write granularity down to single bytes, including a header split mid-way.

vectors.name: meshtastic_header_split_across_chunks
vectors.description: The 4-byte length header itself split 2+2 across writes, then the payload; message completes only after the payload arrives.
vectors.oracle_note: Length becomes readable only once all four header bytes are buffered; declared length 4 gates completion.

vectors.name: meshtastic_payload_split_mid_varint
vectors.description: Header plus the first two payload bytes in one write, remainder in the next; the varint spanning the write boundary reassembles to 69420.
vectors.oracle_note: Base-128 groups 0xac (cont.) and 0x9e (cont.), 0x04 (final) reunite across the boundary.

vectors.name: meshtastic_truncated_stays_buffered_then_completes
vectors.description: Header declares 10 payload bytes but only 6 arrive: no message and nothing lost; the final 4 bytes complete exactly the declared length (xmodem_packet of eight 0x41 bytes).
vectors.oracle_note: Declared length 0x000a; payload 32 08 + eight 41 bytes is field 6 length-delim 8 bytes by protobuf wire rules; truncation must hold the fragment until complete.

vectors.name: meshtastic_back_to_back_boundary_inside_second_header
vectors.description: First message plus the first half of the second message's header in one write; the second write carries the rest. Both messages emerge in order.
vectors.oracle_note: Trailing bytes beyond declared length 4 belong to the next message and must be preserved; second header 03000000 declares 3 bytes (18 d2 09 = field 3 varint 1234).

vectors.name: meshtastic_zero_length_message
vectors.description: A header declaring zero payload bytes completes immediately and yields a ToRadio with no payload variant set (an empty protobuf message is legal).
vectors.oracle_note: Declared length 0 satisfies completion with an empty payload; protobuf parsing of empty bytes leaves every optional variant unset.

vectors.name: meshtastic_disconnect_discards_partial
vectors.description: A fragment left mid-message is dropped on disconnect; after reconnect a fresh message parses cleanly.
vectors.oracle_note: Reassembly state is reset on connection loss; the orphaned '18 ac' fragment must not leak into the new connection's stream.

vectors.name: meshtastic_outbound_oversized_rejected
vectors.description: Queueing an outbound FromRadio whose serialization is 603 bytes (> meshtastic_max_message_size 512) is rejected with an error, not silently truncated.
vectors.oracle_note: Serialized size hand-computed: field 4 length-delim tag 0x22 (1) + varint 600 = d8 04 (2) + 600 payload bytes = 603 > 512 limit.

vectors.name: meshtastic_parse_ble_message_valid
vectors.description: parse_ble_message over header+payload returns the payload and total consumed length.
vectors.oracle_note: Declared length 4 consumes 4 header + 4 payload.

vectors.name: meshtastic_parse_ble_message_truncated
vectors.description: Header declaring 16 bytes with only 2 present raises a truncation error.
vectors.oracle_note: Declared 0x0010 vs 2 available bytes.

vectors.name: meshtastic_parse_ble_message_too_short
vectors.description: Fewer than 4 bytes cannot contain the header and raise a length error.
vectors.oracle_note: Header is fixed at 4 bytes.
